 UFC Doha: Prochazka vs. Stirling features a compelling flyweight rematch on the prelims as ranked contender Amir Albazi meets surging Brazilian finisher Alessandro Costa nearly four years after their first meeting. Check out our UFC Doha odds series for our Albazi-Costa prediction and pick.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Amir Albazi (17-3) desperately needs a bounce-back performance after dropping two straight unanimous decisions against top-five flyweight opposition. The Iraqi contender was outpointed by Kyoji Horiguchi in February after previously losing a five-round unanimous decision to former champion Brandon Moreno as he comes into his fight this weekend against Alessandro Costa.
 Alessandro Costa (17-5) arrives in Doha red-hot on a three-fight finish streak that earned him this long-awaited rematch. He submitted Cody Durden via rear-naked choke at UFC 329 in July after previously finishing Matt Schnell with first-round punches in June as he comes into his fight this weekend against Amir Albazi.

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement UFC Doha Odds: Amir Albazi-Alessandro Costa Odds 
 Amir Albazi: -108
 Alessandro Costa: -112
 Over 2.5 rounds: -180
 Under 2.5 rounds: +140
 Why Amir Albazi Will Win 
 Amir Albazi already owns a knockout victory over Alessandro Costa from their first encounter, giving him proven psychological confidence heading into the rematch. Even during his recent losing skid, Albazi only fell short against elite championship-caliber foes in Brandon Moreno and Kyoji Horiguchi.
 Stepping back down from top-five competition to face an unranked contender gives Albazi a golden chance to reassert his grappling dominance. Albazi is a suffocating Brazilian jiu-jitsu black belt who excels at latching onto the back, controlling wrist ties, and hunting rear-naked chokes once the fight hits the canvas.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Albazi also brings a slight height and reach edge along with tremendous physical strength for the 125-pound division. Against Horiguchi in February, Albazi struggled to close distance on an elusive karate stylist, yet Costa fights far more squarely in the pocket.
 That forward-leaning stance gives Albazi clearer opportunities to time counter punches or duck underneath hooks for reactive takedowns. If Albazi stays composed, avoids brawling recklessly, and reestablishes his wrestling early, his pedigree should carry him through.
 Controlling top position and shutting down Costa's surging rhythm can put "The Prince" right back into the flyweight contender mix.
 Why Alessandro Costa Will Win 
 Alessandro Costa looks like a completely transformed fighter compared to the short-notice debutant Albazi knocked out nearly four years ago. Riding three consecutive 2026 stoppages over Stewart Nicoll, Matt Schnell, and Cody Durden, Costa enters with overwhelming momentum and sharp activity.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While Albazi has gone winless since 2023 and landed just 16 significant strikes across three rounds against Horiguchi, Costa has been finishing opponents in devastating fashion. He boasts seven wins by knockout and seven by submission, proving he can end fights wherever they go.
 Costa's crisp boxing, vicious body shots, and calf kicks present major problems for Albazi's stiff, upright striking defense. Against Cody Durden in July, Costa stuffed both takedown attempts and snatched a rear-naked choke, proving his grappling defense and opportunism have leaped forward.
 At 30 years old, Costa is hitting his athletic prime right as Albazi shows signs of ring rust and declining explosiveness after neck issues and tough decision losses. If Costa keeps his back off the cage and pushes a sharp, high-output pace, Albazi may struggle to keep up.
 With confidence at an all-time high, Costa has all the tools to avenge his debut loss in style.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Final Albazi-Costa Prediction & Pick 
 Alessandro Costa is the pick to avenge his UFC debut loss in one of the tightest toss-ups on the card. Momentum and activity mean everything in MMA, and these two flyweights are traveling in completely opposite directions throughout 2026.
 Click Above to Subscribe Albazi looked noticeably gun-shy and slow against Kyoji Horiguchi in February, landing less than 24 percent of his significant strikes while going 0-for-7 on takedowns. Meanwhile, Costa has fought three times this year and finished every single opponent via body KO, TKO, and submission.
 Albazi's grappling pedigree keeps him dangerous if he scores an early takedown and secures back control. However, Costa's improved takedown defense, crisp body work, and punishing boxing combinations should dictate the exchanges on the feet.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Expect Costa to stuff Albazi's early entries, chew him up with leg kicks and sharp punches, and edge out a hard-fought decision or late stoppage.
 Final Amir Albazi-Alessandro Costa Prediction & Pick: Alessandro Costa (-112), OVER 2.5 rounds (-180)
